perf(export): run the TensorRT INT8 patch embedding as a matrix multiply (#1638)

An INT8 TensorRT engine kept the patch embedding in FP16. As a `Conv` over the 3-channel image it is the one backbone
layer TensorRT cannot run in INT8 without padding its input to 32 channels and storing the added zero channels in the
engine, as a constant that grows with the batch. So `plan_int8` leaves every convolution whose input channels are not a
multiple of 32 in FP16, the patch embedding included.

`int8_source_graph` now rewrites a non-overlapping, ungrouped, unpadded patch `Conv` in the backbone encoder as
`Reshape` -> `Transpose` -> `Reshape` -> `MatMul` (+ bias) -> `Reshape` -> `Transpose`, when its flattened patch
(`channels * patch * patch`) is a multiple of 32. The result is the same sum, written to the `Conv`'s own output tensor,
and the kernel the `Conv` read is dropped when nothing else reads it. The `MatMul` has no channels to pad, so the existing
plan quantizes it with the rest of the backbone. The rewrite is applied to the FP32 graph that is planned and calibrated
and again to the FP16 copy that is quantized; it names the `MatMul` deterministically, and a copy that lacks a node the
plan quantizes is refused.

It applies to the detection models (16-pixel patches, 768 values per patch). The segmentation and keypoint models cut
12-pixel patches of 432 values, which is not a multiple of 32. As a matrix multiply those ran 1.0% faster and 0.4 MB
smaller on Seg Small (a prototype build, same harness), with 0.14 (box) and 0.20 (mask) point more AP loss, against 3.4% to 7.8% faster for the detection
models, so they keep the `Conv` and their exports are unchanged.

Measured on an RTX 5070 (TensorRT 11.4.0.106) against the engines the previous commit builds: the INT8 engines of Nano,
Small, Medium and Large run 3.4% to 7.8% faster per image at batch 1 (CUDA-graph median of 9 rounds of 200) and are 1.2
to 4.3 MB smaller; Nano at batch 8 goes from 49.0 to 36.7 MB. Box AP against FP16 moved by -0.10, +0.08, 0.00 and -0.14
point (differences of the rounded AP-change figures; first 4872 val2017 images for Nano and Small, 2500 for Medium and
Large; calibrated on the last 128 val2017 images). Two builds of the new graph agreed within 0.03 point, so these are
small real effects, the size of moving one MLP layer in or out of INT8 (-0.52 to -0.79 against -0.64 for all layers on
Nano).

Section 8.1 of the CUDA cookbook, run unmodified on this change for the four detection sizes (5000 val2017 images, 128
train2017 calibration images, 15 rounds of 200), replaces their RTX 5070 rows in the docs: speed-up over FP16 at batch 1
with a CUDA graph 1.40x, 1.34x, 1.27x and 1.15x (was 1.28x, 1.26x, 1.16x, 1.12x), box AP change -0.70, -0.67, -0.91 and
-0.62 (was -0.60, -0.60, -0.86, -0.55), INT8 engine 0.53x to 0.79x of the FP16 one over all sizes and batches (was 0.66x
to 0.79x). The Tesla T4 detection rows were not re-measured and say so.

* test(export): loosen the float32 tolerance of the patch-embedding equivalence test
* docs(export): re-measure the Tesla T4 detection rows with the INT8 patch embedding

+        >>> _drop_unread_initializers(graph, ["old", "x"])
+        >>> [init.name for init in graph.initializer]
+        ['x']
+    """
+    read = {name for nested in _iter_graphs(graph) for node in nested.node for name in node.input}
+    read |= {value.name for value in (*graph.input, *graph.output)}

+def _patch_embedding_as_matmul(model: Any) -> int:
+    """Rewrite the backbone's patch-embedding ``Conv`` as a ``MatMul`` over flattened patches, in place.
+
+    TensorRT pads a convolution's 3 input channels, and stores the padding in the engine (see
+    :func:`_pads_input_channels`), so the patch embedding is the one backbone layer that has to stay FP16 as a ``Conv``.
+    As a matrix multiply over ``channels * patch * patch`` values per patch (768 for an RGB image and 16-pixel patches)
+    it has nothing to pad and runs in INT8 like the other backbone layers. The two compute the same sum.
+
+    Only a ``Conv`` inside the backbone encoder that :func:`_pads_input_channels` would keep FP16 and that
+    :func:`_patch_kernel` and :func:`_patch_image` accept is rewritten: RF-DETR's detection models (16-pixel patches),
+    not its segmentation and keypoint models (12-pixel patches, 432 values per patch). The shape inference that finds
+    the image size runs only when such a ``Conv`` exists. A kernel that is also a graph input is left alone, since it
+    can be replaced at run time. The kernel of a replaced ``Conv`` is dropped when nothing else reads it (one reached
+    through an ``Identity`` alias is kept). The rewrite is deterministic for a given name, so applying it to the FP32
+    graph that is planned and calibrated and to the FP16 graph that is quantized yields the same ``MatMul`` name.
+
+    Args:
+        model: ``ModelProto`` to rewrite; left untouched when it holds no such layer.
+
+    Returns:
+        The number of layers rewritten.
+    """
+    import onnx
+    from onnx import numpy_helper
+
+    graph = model.graph
+    initializers = _constant_weights(graph)
+    counts = Counter(node.name for node in graph.node)
+    overridable = {value.name for value in graph.input}  # a kernel listed here can be replaced at run time
+    candidates = [
+        (node, kernel)
+        for node in graph.node
+        if node.op_type == "Conv"
+        and node.name.startswith(_BACKBONE_ENCODER)
+        and counts[node.name] == 1
+        and node.input[1] not in overridable
+        and _weight_name(node, initializers)
+        and _pads_input_channels(node, initializers)
+        and (kernel := _patch_kernel(node, initializers))
+    ]
+    if not candidates:
+        return 0
+    inferred = onnx.shape_inference.infer_shapes(model)
+    shapes = {v.name: v for v in (*inferred.graph.value_info, *inferred.graph.input, *inferred.graph.output)}
+    taken, node_names = _tensor_names(graph), set(counts)
+    replacements: dict[str, list[Any]] = {}
+    for conv, kernel in candidates:
+        patches = _patch_image(_dims(shapes, conv.input[0]), kernel)
+        matmul_name = f"{conv.name.rsplit('/', 1)[0]}/MatMul"
+        if patches is None or matmul_name in node_names:
+            continue
+        weight = numpy_helper.to_array(initializers[conv.input[1]])
+        replacements[conv.name] = _patch_matmul_nodes(conv, matmul_name, patches, graph, weight, taken, node_names)
+    if replacements:
+        kernels = [conv.input[1] for conv, _ in candidates if conv.name in replacements]
+        ordered = [new for node in graph.node for new in replacements.get(node.name, [node])]
+        del graph.node[:]
+        graph.node.extend(ordered)
+        _drop_unread_initializers(graph, kernels)
+    return len(replacements)

+def _patch_embedding(
+    *,
+    channels: int = 3,
+    patch: int = 16,
+    size: int = 32,
+    out_channels: int = 8,
+    bias: bool = True,
+    empty_bias: bool = False,
+    prefix: str = BACKBONE,
+    batch: int = 1,
+    height: int | str | None = None,
+    width: int | None = None,
+    kernel: tuple[int, int] | None = None,
+    **attributes: Any,
+) -> Any:
+    """Build ``image -> Conv -> features`` as a patch embedding: kernel and stride *kernel*, no padding.
+
+    Args:
+        channels: Input channels of the image.
+        patch: Kernel size and stride, in pixels, when *kernel* is not given.
+        size: Image height and width, unless *height* or *width* is given.
+        out_channels: Output channels of the kernel.
+        bias: Give the ``Conv`` a bias.
+        empty_bias: Name the bias input with an empty string, how ONNX spells an omitted optional input.
+        prefix: Node-name prefix of the ``Conv``.
+        batch: Batch size of the image.
+        height: Overrides the declared image height; a string makes it symbolic.
+        width: Overrides the declared image width.
+        kernel: ``(rows, columns)`` of a rectangular kernel and stride.
+        **attributes: ``Conv`` attributes that replace the patch-embedding ones.
+
+    Returns:
+        A checked-shape ``ModelProto`` whose output ``features`` is the ``Conv``'s output.
+
+    Examples:
+        >>> model = _patch_embedding(channels=2, patch=4, size=8)
+        >>> [node.op_type for node in model.graph.node], model.graph.output[0].name
+        (['Conv'], 'features')
+    """
+    rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
+    rows, columns = kernel or (patch, patch)
+    high, wide = height or size, width or size
+    inits = [
+        numpy_helper.from_array(rng.standard_normal((out_channels, channels, rows, columns)).astype(np.float32), "w")
+    ]
+    inputs = ["image", "w"]
+    if bias:
+        inits.append(numpy_helper.from_array(rng.standard_normal(out_channels).astype(np.float32), "b"))
+        inputs.append("b")
+    elif empty_bias:

+    conv = {"kernel_shape": [rows, columns], "strides": [rows, columns], **attributes}
+    grid = ["out_height" if isinstance(high, str) else high // rows, wide // columns]
+    graph = helper.make_graph(

+        "patch_embedding",
+        [helper.make_tensor_value_info("image", TensorProto.FLOAT, [batch, channels, high, wide])],
+        [helper.make_tensor_value_info("features", TensorProto.FLOAT, [batch, out_channels, *grid])],
+        inits,

+    """Make *model*'s ``features`` the source of ``dets`` and ``labels`` and return it, so that INT8 accepts the graph.
